newsitem.title: USA: California football deal to cost Alameda, Oakland.
newsitem.headline: California football deal to cost Alameda, Oakland.

text.p: Oakland and Alameda County will have to pay out an estimated $8 million next fiscal year to cover debt payments on a $200 million coliseum bond deal, county officials warned on Monday.

The Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum Authority said in a quarterly report that revenues generated from the Raiders football stadium project "may not be sufficient to pay the full debt service on the stadium bonds."
As a result, the city of Oakland and Alameda County are each expected to contribute $4 million in the 1997-1998 fiscal year to help cover bond payments, the authority's report said.
The authority issued the bonds to lure the National Football League Raiders back to Oakland and to pay for coliseum improvements.
The bonds were expected to be paid off through the sale of 10-year personal seat licenses, club seats and other revenues.
But sales of seats and other stadium products have fallen $32 million short of projections and stadium construction costs have exceeded the budget by $30 million.
Due to these problems, some local elected officials are calling for an overhaul of the bond deal to make it easier for the city and county to repay investors.
Later this week, the Alameda County Grand Jury is expected to issue a report based on its investigation of the bond deal.
